spurt2_domain_findings.claim: 'Human approved' usually means TACIT approval, not affirmation, and the two cannot be reliably distinguished. MAINTAINER FRAMING (2026-09-15, supersedes the earlier 'auto-approval' wording): the common case is not a machine inventing an opinion -- it is the ordinary interlinear workflow. A person works a text, interacts with one or more parts of an analysis, never clicks the approve check; the analysis is now in use in a segment, and ParseFiler records approval on their behalf at the next filing run.
spurt2_domain_findings.citation: FieldWorks/Src/LexText/ParserCore/ParseFiler.cs:302-320, SetUnsuccessfulParseEvals. Comment at :310 reads 'ensure that used analyses have a user evaluation'; :311 does m_userAgent.SetEvaluation(analysis, Opinions.approves) when the analysis (or one of its glosses) appears in wordform.OccurrencesBag segment analyses -- and it fires BEFORE the noopinion/delete check at :313-318.
spurt2_domain_findings.scope_correction: BROADER than first reported. SetUnsuccessfulParseEvals is called on BOTH result branches at ParseFiler.cs:231 (ErrorMessage != null) and :238 (successful parse), for every wordform whose Checksum changed. So this is not a failure-path quirk -- every filing run writes user approvals across all processed wordforms.
consequences: HumanApprovedAnalyses means 'affirmed OR tacit', with no way to split it. Same agent, same Opinions.approves, no flag and no separate timestamp recording which path wrote it.

Tacit approval is NOT nothing -- leaving an analysis standing in a text you are working through is a real but weak human signal. The spec must not describe it as noise or as a bug. It is simply not the act the oracle needs: nothing was affirmed about the morphology.

The segment join is ONE-SIDED. Approved + not in any segment = affirmed, reliably. Approved + in a segment = affirmed OR tacit, unknowable -- a person who genuinely clicked approve on a word in their text lands in the same bucket. So the split is reported as {affirmed, indeterminate}, NEVER {affirmed, tacit}: labelling an individual analysis tacit claims a provenance the database does not record.
The single_probe_note is measuring the wrong thing: a user-noopinion count is NOT 'never human-reviewed', because in-segment analyses were silently upgraded out of noopinion.

Protective corollary for P0-1: in-segment analyses are shielded from the non-undoable delete. Weak evidence, strong shield -- the right asymmetry on a non-undoable path. The deletion set is the conjunction 'user-noopinion AND not in any segment'.
